Elena (PM): Quick sync — we need to finalize the response envelope for next release. Primary asks from customers: token breakdown, stable trace ids for debugging, and minimal cost metadata. Can we agree on field names + migration plan?

Alex Chen (Eng-API): I'd propose a small, explicit envelope: request_id (uuid), trace_id (trace/span id), and a usage block. wire format should be snake_case to match existing endpoints. Keep names stable for SDK mapping.

Maya Gupta (Eng-Runtime): +1 on compact. For tokens: total_tokens, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens. Runtime can emit estimated_cost_micros (int) for per-call cost. We should avoid anything that inflates the payload size.

Samir Patel (Eng-ML): For model-level accuracy we sometimes have extra internal counts, but I think a standard set for API consumers is best. Suggest naming: prompt_tokens / completion_tokens (explicit), and add tokens_per_second only in telemetry (not returned).

Priya Rao (Security): Heads up — do NOT include the prompt text in any returned metadata by default. Also need to add a retention and opt-in note for token-level logging. Default retention 30d, longer only with explicit opt-in and legal review.

Alex Chen (Eng-API): Example envelope for alignment (inline JSON):
```
{
  "request_id": "9f3b2a8e-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-abcdef123456",
  "trace_id": "00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01",
  "model": "redwood-1.3",
  "usage": {
    "prompt_tokens": 63,
    "completion_tokens": 142,
    "total_tokens": 205,
    "estimated_cost_micros": 12345
  },
  "flags": {
    "cached": false,
    "model_fallback": "redwood-1.2"
  }
}
```

Alex Chen (Eng-API): Notes: prefer snake_case on the wire; SDKs should map to camelCase (e.g., requestId) to match language idioms. Include a header for schema versioning: `X-Rw-Resp-Schema-Version: v1`.

Maya Gupta (Eng-Runtime): How do we handle tool/function calls where each tool returns its own tokens? We could nest per-tool usage under usage.tools: [{"name":"search","prompt_tokens":10,...}]. That keeps the top-level compact while preserving detail.

Samir Patel (Eng-ML): Agreed — nested list for tools seems fine. Keep tool names short and consistent. We should also provide an opt-in detailed_metrics flag for customers who want per-step breakdowns.

Priya Rao (Security): Also log an anonymized trace sample for debugging, but ensure we strip PII and make sampling opt-in for customers in regulated industries.

infra-bot: New spec draft posted to /docs/api/response-envelope-v1.md — please review.

Elena (PM): Next: launch criteria. Must have: 1) spec doc, 2) SDK mapping PRs (python, js), 3) runtime emits the fields in canary, 4) docs + migration guide, 5) rollout plan (canary -> 25% -> 100%). Any objections to that checklist?

Alex Chen (Eng-API): Sounds good. Suggest adding a regression test that asserts usage fields present and types.

Maya Gupta (Eng-Runtime): We'll add a feature flag `resp_schema_v1` for canary. Runtime can default to v1 for internal tests only.

Samir Patel (Eng-ML): I'll add a short eval to confirm token counts align with model tokenizer across a few prompt buckets.

Priya Rao (Security): I'll draft the retention and opt-in language for the docs and send to legal.

Elena (PM): Action items: Alex -> spec updates + SDK mapping plan; Maya -> runtime canary + tool usage shape; Samir -> eval; Priya -> compliance language. Target: spec ready by EOD Friday, canary next week.

Alex Chen (Eng-API): ACK. I'll open the spec PR today and add a small migration section for older clients.

Maya Gupta (Eng-Runtime): ACK, will slot runtime work into next sprint.

Samir Patel (Eng-ML): ACK.

Priya Rao (Security): ACK.

Elena (PM): Great — thanks all. :shipit:
